close_reason: Expanded SharingBackend::update_object rustdoc to match the .19 destroy_object / .33 create_object contract template. Added: Error contract (NotFound/Forbidden/InvalidPatch/InvalidProperties/OverQuota/WillDestroy/serverFail with RFC 8620 §5.3 anchors and handler-mapping references), State-mutation contract (state-counter + change-log atomicity, plus explicit clause that Ok(None) is a wire-shape signal not a no-op), Idempotency clause, and corrected the generic-method type-scope (was 'an existing Principal', now correctly 'an existing object of type O' with a note that the current handler short-circuits ShareNotification per RFC 9670 §3.3). clippy clean. fmt clean. Doc warnings unchanged (only 2 pre-existing JMAP-23su intra-doc-link warnings, not introduced by this change).
description:
**Location**: `crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/backend.rs:132-143`.

**The gap**: `SharingBackend::update_object`'s rustdoc says:

> Apply a partial update (patch) to an existing Principal.
>
> Returns `Some(updated_object)` if the backend modified any properties
> beyond what the client requested (RFC 8620 §5.3 server-set field echo),
> or `None` if the patch was applied verbatim.

That is the entirety of the doc. By contrast, `destroy_object` (lines
145-198) carries a full contract block: explicit error mapping for
NotFound / Forbidden / Other-storage-failure, an explicit
"state-mutation contract" section guaranteeing the state counter and
change-log advance atomically with the mutation, and an "idempotency"
note. `update_object` has NONE of these. A consumer reading the trait
sees no answer to:

1. **Error contract**: which `SetErrorType`s does the handler accept
   here? RFC 8620 §5.3 admits at least `notFound`, `forbidden`,
   `invalidPatch`, `invalidProperties`, `overQuota`, `willDestroy`,
   `singleton`. The handler at `principal.rs:181-216` accepts any
   `BackendSetError::SetError(...)` and forwards verbatim, so the
   backend has wide latitude — but the trait doc gives the implementor
   no guidance on which variant maps to which failure mode. By contrast
   `destroy_object` documents `NotFound` for missing id, `Forbidden`
   for permission failure, `Other` for storage failure.

2. **State-mutation contract**: must `get_state::<O>` advance only on
   successful commit? Must `get_changes::<O>` record an `updated` entry
   atomically? The `destroy_object` doc mandates both; the
   `update_object` doc is silent. The reference impl
   (`memory.rs:643-711`) does the right thing, but a downstream
   implementor has no normative source to consult.

3. **Permission enforcement (backend-canonical rule)**: the workspace
   AGENTS.md "Permission enforcement: backend canonical" rule says the
   backend MUST re-verify atomically. The `destroy_object` doc
   restates this; the `update_object` doc does not. A downstream
   implementor who reads only `update_object`'s doc may miss that they
   are the canonical enforcement point for per-object update
   permission.

4. **Account-exists contract**: `destroy_object` doc explicitly says
   the handler pre-checks `account_exists` and the backend MAY treat
   the account as verified-to-exist but defense-in-depth is
   RECOMMENDED. `update_object` doc says nothing — and the reference
   impl in fact does the same defense-in-depth re-check (memory.rs:658-662)
   but with no contract anchor.

5. **Doc body mismatches the generic signature**: "Apply a partial
   update (patch) to an existing **Principal**" — but the method is
   generic over `O: SetObject`, which can be `Principal` OR
   `ShareNotification`. For `ShareNotification` the handler at
   `notification.rs:106-113` short-circuits with `forbidden` before
   reaching the backend, so the type-confusion is benign in the
   current handler set, but the trait doc must not promise
   `Principal`-specific semantics on a generic method.

**Why this matters as a contract finding**: a downstream backend
implementor reading `update_object`'s doc currently has no normative
source for any of (1)-(4) and is implicitly told (5) the wrong
type-scope. They will guess; some guesses produce silent wire
breakage (state-advance-on-failure-path makes /changes consumers see
phantom updates; missing permission re-check ships a security bug).

**Parallel finding**: bd:JMAP-3t94.19 covers the identical gap on
`destroy_object` and was closed by adding the contract block now
present at backend.rs:145-198. The fix here is the same shape:
expand `update_object`'s doc to mirror that contract block,
type-corrected to the generic `O`.

**Cookie-cutter propagation**: every extension-server sibling has a
`SharingBackend`-equivalent trait with the same generic `update_object`.
If this gap exists here it likely exists in chat, calendars, contacts,
filenode, metadata, tasks. The canonical mail-server is the
authoritative shape — a propagation pass should look there first.
title: SharingBackend::update_object underspecified — no error contract, no state-mutation contract, doc body mismatches generic signature
